ai.description: This snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow-orange nuchal collar and black-bordered red or yellow spots along the neck. It features keeled scales and a dark subocular streak.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Himalayan Keelback is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow or orange nuchal collar located immediately behind the head, which contrasts sharply with its dark body.
ai.habitat: The Himalayan Keelback inhabits moist, temperate forests and scrublands in the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Keelback is primarily diurnal, often foraging for amphibians and fish near mountain streams and damp forest floors during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhabdophis himalayanus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatching observed in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Himalayan Keelback occurs in the Himalayas across Northern India (Himachal Pradesh to Arunachal Pradesh) and Nepal, typically at elevations between 1,000 and 3,000 meters.
